scope: Two-party local demo: Alice and Bob each run their own app with only their own private roots, isolated by macOS sandbox-exec on one host. Isolated Zebra NU7 regtest and Anvil. Not independent administration, not a public network.
implementation: scripts/two_party.py (network, relay, launcher), scripts/party_app.py (owner app over latch_operator.py), web/party.* and web/network.*

isolation.policy: each app process tree: deny file-read*/file-write* on the other owner roots, the relay store and the network store
isolation.proof: at launch, under each app policy, reading the other owner identity file raises PermissionError (both directions); shown as isolation_proven on the network page

relay.field_audit: only identity public keys/certificates, quote and acceptance signatures, full terms, consent signatures, digests and txids; no receive address, viewing key, witness, note data or nonce

success_with_crash.flow: trust both ways -> Alice quote -> Bob accept (signer online) -> Alice prepare (local faucet, DKG and presign over TLS) -> Bob consent -> Alice consent and fund -> Bob lock -> Alice claim (t public) -> Bob app SIGKILLed -> Alice withdraw -> Bob app restarted -> Bob ZEC claim confirmed and decrypted

refund.flow: ... -> Bob lock -> Alice does not claim -> network advances ETH time -> Bob refund and withdraw -> network mines past the refund height -> Alice native refund confirmed and decrypted
refund.driver: scratch script calling the same /api/act endpoints the pages use

receiver_privacy: check_receiver_privacy.py: 0 receiving FVKs in both workspaces
network_restart: network stopped and started again: Anvil state and escrow restored at the same address; apps resumed from their own files
limits: the network process is a stand-in that mines regtest on demand and exposes labelled time controls
